title: Sections of arbitrary smooth scheme morphisms are regular immersions
statement: Let $X,S$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $f:X\to S$ be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $s:S\to X$ be a morphism satisfying $f\circ s=\operatorname{id}_S$. Then $s$ is an immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. At each $t\in S$ there is an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq X$ of $s(t)$ such that $s^{-1}(U)\to U$ is a closed immersion whose ideal is locally generated by a finite regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. More explicitly, $U$ can be chosen affine, $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, with $s^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}(A/(a_1,\ldots,a_r))$ over $U$, where multiplication by $a_k$ is injective on $A/(a_1,\ldots,a_{k-1})$ and $A/(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\ne0$. The integer $r\ge0$ may vary with $t$, and the empty sequence is allowed. No Noetherian, separation, quasi-compactness, or constant-relative-dimension hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: The identity of $S$ is an immersion (a closed immersion with zero ideal). Apply [lem-zl-immersion-cancellation] to $S\xrightarrow{s}X\xrightarrow{f}S$, whose composite is this identity. Thus $s$ is an immersion. By [def-weil-closed-immersion] choose an open $W\subseteq X$ through which $s$ factors as a closed immersion $S\hookrightarrow W$.

source.place: Tag 067R, lemma-section-smooth-regular-immersion, first two sentences of proof; cancellation is Tag 07RK(1).

proof.text: Fix $t\in S$. Choose an affine open $T=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ containing $t$ and an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq W\cap f^{-1}(T)$ containing $s(t)$. Put $Z=s^{-1}(V)$. Restricting the closed immersion $S\hookrightarrow W$ to $V$ gives $Z\hookrightarrow V$; its affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion] gives $Z=\operatorname{Spec}C$ and a surjection $\varphi:A\to C$. The equality $fs=1$ shows that the restricted map $Z\to T$ is its open inclusion, and that $\varphi$ is an $R$-algebra map. In particular $t\in Z$, and the prime $Q\subseteq A$ of $s(t)$ contains $I=\ker\varphi$.

source.place: Tag 067R, closed-immersion reduction; affine neighbourhood choice as in Tag 063W, lemma-fibre-quasi-regular, proof.

proof.text: The restricted map $V\to T$ is smooth: the finite-presentation condition is local on these open neighbourhoods, and an infinitesimal lift furnished by formal smoothness of $f$ lands in $V$ whenever its restriction does, since a nilpotent thickening has the same underlying points [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. The open inclusion $Z\to T$ is smooth by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition], applied to this inclusion followed by $1_T$ (the identity satisfies the smoothness definition). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] to these two morphisms of affine schemes. It follows that both $R\to A$ and $R\to C$ are smooth ring maps. This verifies the two separate smoothness hypotheses needed next.

source.place: Tags 067R and 067U, lemma-immersion-smooth-into-smooth-regular-immersion, affine smooth source and target; affine translation: morphisms.tex Tag 01V6 and more-morphisms.tex Tag 02H6.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-smooth-quotient-regular-sequence] to the commutative $R$-algebras $A,C$, the surjection $\varphi$, and $Q\supseteq I$. Obtain $g\in A\setminus Q$ such that $IA_g$ is generated by a finite $A_g$-regular list $a_1,\ldots,a_r$. Here the cited statement permits arbitrary coefficient rings, a zero kernel, and an empty list; it requires no relative-dimension bound.

source.place: Tag 067T, lemma-immersion-lci-into-smooth-regular-immersion, smooth affine specialization via Tag 063W(2); reuse of the existing affine kernel node.

proof.text: Take $U=D_V(g)=\operatorname{Spec}A_g$. Then $s(t)\in U$, and $s^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}C_{\varphi(g)}$. The map $A_g\to C_{\varphi(g)}$ is surjective: lift the numerator of each fraction using $\varphi$. Its kernel is $IA_g$: if $\varphi(a)/\varphi(g)^n=0$, some $m$ has $\varphi(g)^m\varphi(a)=0$, so $g^m a\in I$ and $a/g^n\in IA_g$; the reverse containment is immediate. Thus the restricted section is the quotient closed immersion $\operatorname{Spec}(A_g/(a_1,\ldots,a_r))\hookrightarrow U$. By [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] its successive multiplications are injective and its final quotient is nonzero (also witnessed by $t\in s^{-1}U$). This proves every local clause. The choice is made separately for each $t$, so $r$ can vary; if $S$ is empty there are no local clauses to check.
